# Documents

Each document under docs/ says in its front matter what it is (scripts/src/bin/docs.rs). Superseded ones
are left out here; each names what replaced it. docs/upstream/ holds others' text, as fetched.

## Current

How blaze is now. Kept true: CI checks their links, paths and settings against the tree.

- [agents.md](agents.md): blaze for coding agents: `blaze agents install|status|remove` wires Claude Code and Codex to blaze (a hook after each edit that says the new errors and warnings, a hook before each shell command that steers cargo and rustc to blaze, and a block of instructions); `blaze agents hook` is that hook; `blaze diagnostics --since` is the request under it, for any agent; `blaze doctor` says whether all of it is installed and current.
- [benchmarks.md](benchmarks.md): How long an edit takes to build, the memory and disk it uses and how fast its programs run, against cargo, on three platforms.
- [borrowck.md](borrowck.md): blaze's own borrow checker (hir-ty-borrowck): how it matches rustc's verdicts, how it is scored, what is left.
- [cargo.md](cargo.md): Every blaze command and setting: cargo's commands and flags, what a build does, sandboxing, manifests.
- [client.md](client.md): Reaching the daemon with no process launch (blaze-client from Rust, its C ABI, the Node-API addon for TypeScript, the small `blaze-fast` command line), and the thin `blaze`, the small program a no-op build or run costs one round trip through.
- [compiletest.md](compiletest.md): rustc's own test suites under blaze: which suites run and why, what is compared, the pinned corpus, the ratchet.
- [const.md](const.md): Const evaluation: blaze's own interpreter for constants and const fns, and what it covers.
- [contributing.md](contributing.md): How to build, test and change blaze: AI use, where new code goes, rules for code, working in parallel, landing.
- [fuzzing.md](fuzzing.md): The fuzzers: generated programs and edits, each held to blaze's own build from nothing (a warm daemon, a warm store), what a finding is, and what they do not cover.
- [gc.md](gc.md): What blaze removes from disk and when: the collector of build dirs, shared std stores, temporaries and trash; the pacer that works harder as a volume fills, leases, records, roots and the grace, and why nothing in use is removed; the daemon's store under the home's budget, its pins and what a build says of it.
- [harness.md](harness.md): The harnesses that test blaze (real crates' own tests, and blaze held to itself), what each checks, and how CI runs them.
- [install.md](install.md): Installing blaze: the install script, the release channels and what gets installed.
- [ix-prof.md](ix-prof.md): Profiling any Rust program, not only blaze, like Go's pprof. Covers the ix-prof crate (CPU samples of every thread, tracing spans with their own CPU time and allocations, named waits, allocations by stack), `IX_PROF=<dir>`, the loopback `/debug/pprof` endpoint and live stream, and `blaze pprof` with top, peek, tree, list, flame, diff, export and --http.
- [lints.md](lints.md): The general `blaze::` lints `blaze check` runs in every workspace (`blaze::general`): what each catches, why it costs, how to fix or allow it, and the `clippy.toml` keys that tune them; then the three guard lints of `blaze::internal` that ask for a stated reason on the line (`durable_write`, `unbounded_wait`, `combined_identity`), and `implicit_allocator`, which no comment keeps: don't allocate where a borrow or a buffer does, else name the allocator, `Global` included, with a fix to the explicit form; the gate counts the `// alloc:` lines left to convert and the explicit `Global` uses.
- [macos.md](macos.md): Which macOS interfaces blaze uses where a private, undocumented or Apple-only call beats the portable one (rule macos-private-apis), what each buys, its risk, and what is still to measure.
- [mir-passes.md](mir-passes.md): The MIR passes from built MIR to runtime MIR, ported from rustc, that codegen and the interpreter run on.
- [no-rustc.md](no-rustc.md): The no-rustc rule, what counts as running rustc, the end state, and the live list of the places that still name rustc or cargo.
- [release.md](release.md): Releases: the canary and stable channels, how a release is cut and what gates promotion to stable.
- [resolve.md](resolve.md): Reading Cargo.toml and .cargo/config.toml as cargo does (blaze-manifest), and how it measured against cargo.
- [terminal.md](terminal.md): What `blaze build`, `run`, `check` and `test` show: on a terminal a region redrawn while a build runs and at most one line when it ends, off one stable `blaze:` lines; and the one sans-IO core (blaze-screen) that makes both from the build's events.
- [toolchain.md](toolchain.md): blaze's own pinned nightly: what it is, how it is fetched and checked, and the daily bump.
- [usage.md](usage.md): Getting started: using blaze on a project, in short.
- [future/harness-chat-library.md](future/harness-chat-library.md): Open and search Harness, Claude and Codex conversations with Command-O.
- [future/harness-model-cues.md](future/harness-model-cues.md): Quiet completion sounds and readable model capability and effort in Harness.
- [future/harness-questions-overlays.md](future/harness-questions-overlays.md): A native question view and Harness-owned hover cards.
- [v2/plan/invariants.md](v2/plan/invariants.md): Every invariant, refinement and reference model blaze states in its code, with the test that checks it and the planted bugs that prove the check; generated by scripts/src/bin/invariants.rs.
- [v2/plan/proofs.md](v2/plan/proofs.md): Every theorem blaze claims is proved in Lean, with its statement as its module states it and its ledger row; generated by harness/v2/lean_gate.py from lean/theorems.json, and held by the gate to the axioms listed.
- [v2/plan/design/astlog-sema.md](v2/plan/design/astlog-sema.md): astlog over blaze's own syntax trees and semantic database: Rust code patterns with `$name` metavariables whose paths match by resolution, demand-driven semantic relations (resolves, type-of, implements, callee, references, enclosing items, in-unsafe, in-test), a semi-naive evaluator shared with the tree-sitter source, and rewrites that go out through blaze-intent. One versioned CBOR request for an edit and one for a read-only query; the CLI is a client of both.
- [v2/plan/design/profile-names.md](v2/plan/design/profile-names.md): The flight recorder names strings per thread. Each thread interns into a private table whose ids are scoped to its own ring, defines each name in the ring the first time it uses it, and starts a new generation at chunk boundaries. Readers turn per-thread ids into global ones as they decode, so the hot path shares nothing and the profile parquet is unchanged.

## Plans

Designs not (fully) built, newest first.

- [v2/plan/design/type-of.md](v2/plan/design/type-of.md) (2026-11-13): "`type_of!(desc)`, a type computed by const code (row Q7 of sql.md; phase 3 of comptime.md). A description is a value of core's `reflect::TypeDesc`; `type_of!` names `<Described<'a, {desc}, Args> as TypeOf>::Type`, an associated type the trait solver normalizes by reading the description's value tree. No new syntax, no new kind of type: a described record is core's `Record`, so identity is by the description's value. blaze-sql's checker runs in a `const static` block and returns a description; a SQL error is the block's panic."
- [v2/plan/design/trust.md](v2/plan/design/trust.md) (2026-11-13): Secure by default for dependencies. Every crate that is not a workspace member is denied `unsafe` and every ambient capability (fs, net, process, env, clock, thread, global state, randomness, FFI, build script, proc macro) unless the root manifest's `[workspace.metadata.blaze.trust]` grants it by name, with a reason and optionally an exact version. The `blaze::trust` lints read this off the effect walk with one shortest witness each; `blaze audit grants` prints the table a workspace needs today. Built is the lint layer; the driver does not pass the grants yet.
- [v2/plan/design/test-selection.md](v2/plan/design/test-selection.md) (2026-11-13): blaze test reruns only the tests that can have changed: a test's result is an outside record keyed by its identity, its asks are the functions it executed and what it read outside, a suite index finds the tests an edit touches, and a no-op is answered by the certificate. One flag runs everything.
- [v2/plan/design/target.md](v2/plan/design/target.md) (2026-11-13): The fresh core. One process per command answers from records keyed from text before the work and filed at the address of what their work read; no daemon, no query graph, no memory admission. Says the scope, the processes, verifying once, the records and their key rules, memory, positions, sharing and remote execution, what is deleted and reused, the order, the floors and how the finished system is judged. Interface crate crates/blaze-keyed.
- [v2/plan/design/sql.md](v2/plan/design/sql.md) (2026-11-13): blaze-sql, typed SQL with no injection. A query is a const string checked at compile time against a schema made of Rust structs; its parameters are named (`$name`), bound by a record, and its row type is computed (`type_of!`). One sans-IO checker (parse, infer, render) in `crates/blaze-sql`, drivers for C SQLite (`crates/blaze-sqlite`) and Postgres (`crates/blaze-pg`, a sans-IO wire protocol). The checker and the drivers are being written; the typed surface waits on three language pieces, each a ledger row.
- [v2/plan/design/sim.md](v2/plan/design/sim.md) (2026-11-13): blaze owns its test engine. A test case is a function of one tape of labelled, bounded choices in which 0 is always the calm choice; `crates/blaze-sim` draws the tape from a seed, shrinks a failing tape to the fewest and smallest choices that still fail, prints it and replays it exactly, and holds the pieces every simulation re-implemented by hand (in-flight answers delivered by choice, planted-bug controls, reach points). Hegel and `vendor/hegeltest` go; `blaze_core::sim::Sim`, the fresh core's simulation and `blaze-check`'s random schedules come to draw from the same tape.
- [v2/plan/design/refined-values.md](v2/plan/design/refined-values.md) (2026-11-13): Correct by construction for values. Narrow integer types, `Int<LO, HI>` as a library over `where const`, `#[blaze::invariant(..)]` on private-field structs, and `requires`/`ensures` that the compiler proves at every site or refuses with the missing relation. One prover (hir-ty-pure's reach, linear facts), one deny lint (`blaze::refinement`), and std measures (`len`) with a table of how std calls change them.
- [v2/plan/design/read-addressed.md](v2/plan/design/read-addressed.md) (2026-11-13): A proposal to change how target.md finds a body, a surface and a unit manifest. Today each is keyed by its text and everything reachable from it by name, with a read list checked and the record copied under a new key when the key moves. Proposed, each is found by what it read, so an unrelated edit moves no key, nothing is refiled or copied, and correctness rests on one claim (the read set is complete) and not two. Says what was found in the code, the change as an outside review amended it, why it is sound, its cost against the floor, and what it does to the crates built on blaze-keyed. Decided (D39); blaze-keyed, blaze-host and blaze-unitkey are built on it and landing on main; blaze-front is not built on main yet.
- [v2/plan/design/loop-match.md](v2/plan/design/loop-match.md) (2026-11-13): lane loop-match: `#[loop_match]` / `#[const_continue]` (feature loop_match) lower a constant state transition to a jump into its arm, past the loop head's chain of arm tests; malformed uses are refused with rustc's messages.
- [v2/plan/design/lazy-file-ids.md](v2/plan/design/lazy-file-ids.md) (2026-11-13): A file of a head is stamped when the watcher sees it and hashed only when a build first reads it, streamed in a 64 KiB buffer on the pool; its bytes go to the store once and the tree, the journal and the image name it by content ID, so no file size is bounded by a 32-bit record and the main thread never hashes.
- [v2/plan/design/implied-bounds.md](v2/plan/design/implied-bounds.md) (2026-11-13): "Two opt-in gates. blaze_implied_bounds: the bounds a type or trait declares hold in every function, impl and trait whose header names it (struct C<A: X> gives impl<A> C<A> the bound A: X). blaze_anon_params: a `_` type argument in a function's parameter types or an impl's header is a parameter of its own, bounded by its position (fn len<T>(v: &Vec<T, _>)); it turns on implied bounds."
- [v2/plan/design/host.md](v2/plan/design/host.md) (2026-11-13): The host of the keyed driver. blaze-keyed's driver decides what a request does (certificate, then a mark per unit, then records found by what they read); blaze-host performs its effects on a real store and pool with a Front it is given. This page says the three crates (blaze-unitkey, blaze-front, blaze-host), what each task reads and writes, and each operation's floor.
- [v2/plan/design/front-end-on-memo.md](v2/plan/design/front-end-on-memo.md) (2026-11-13): Port base-db, hir-expand, hir-def, hir-ty, hir-ty-pure, hir-ty-mir and every crate above them from blaze-query's tracked engine to blaze-memo, in one batch with no second path. It covers the eight rules with site counts, the hard cases, nine write-only lanes, the compile order with its gates, what is deleted, and the cost of each edit-loop operation against its floor.
- [v2/plan/design/effect-summary.md](v2/plan/design/effect-summary.md) (2026-11-13): One interprocedural effect summary per monomorphized instance (hir-ty-pure's walk, extended with sync and lock kinds, the lock classes taken, held-while-taking edges and guards held across a block), and the lints on it - loop_turn_effects and sync_on_answer_path (deny, on marked functions), lock_order and lock_across_wait (internal, allowed) - with no_alloc served by the existing noalloc.
- [v2/plan/design/claims.md](v2/plan/design/claims.md) (2026-11-13): A promise in a doc comment is derived by the compiler, checked by an attribute, or points at what proves it; never only asserted. The one written form (`# Guarantees` / `# Invariants` items ending in `Evidence:` or `Unverified:`), the six lints that enforce it in crates/blaze-lints (`claims/`), and the ledger in scripts/src/bin/invariants.rs that lists every claim with its evidence and level and that the gate holds.
- [v2/plan/design/audit.md](v2/plan/design/audit.md) (2026-11-13): Dependencies are untrusted by default. A git source builds only from a tree whose BLAKE3 digest `blaze.lock` pins, since a SHA-1 commit id is no pin. `blaze audit` checks every locked package against a pinned RustSec database and against yanked versions, and every source for a strong pin, with one finding per package and reason, each with its chain, fix and manifest line.
- [v2/plan/design/proved-unreachable.md](v2/plan/design/proved-unreachable.md) (2026-11-12): "blaze::unreachable!(): a site the compiler must prove no path reaches, by one abstract interpretation of a function's MIR (known variants, integer bounds, length relations, nonzero); the same proof takes dead panic sites off what #[blaze::nopanic] and the panic lints count. Also blaze::todo: a typed hole that warns locally and is an error in the merge gate and a release."
- [v2/plan/design/on-save.md](v2/plan/design/on-save.md) (2026-11-12): "A save is built when the watcher commits it, not when a command asks (lane onsave-1112) - the daemon sends itself the checkout's last build or check, exactly as its client sent it, on a connection of its own; one such build at a time, never beside a request's; a request for the same thing waits for it and then walks, any other request cancels it and goes on at once. Built, behind `BLAZE_AHEAD=1` - the decisions are a sans-IO core (`serve/ahead.rs`) with a schedule test and four planted bugs. Not built - the default, battery and load signals, a barrier on macOS that needs no flush. The watcher's flush stays on every request; when it could go is said here."
- [v2/plan/design/no-global-heap.md](v2/plan/design/no-global-heap.md) (2026-11-12): bstd programs run with no global heap. The `#[global_allocator]` is a refuser; each of bstd's 94 `// alloc:` sites moves to the owner of its lifetime (the world, a task's frame, a request's frame, a registered span); a test runs every bstd example under the refuser.
- [v2/plan/design/launcher.md](v2/plan/design/launcher.md) (2026-11-12): "How a program runs under the `edit` goal (D18, D21) - a launcher in the program's own process places code records behind one slot word a function, appends and never overwrites, retires old bodies by per-thread epochs, takes an edit as one gated transaction, and is to run many tests in one process as domains. Built - steps 1 and 2 (`crates/blaze-launch`, `crates/blaze-launch-rt`), step 3 (tier 0 code that calls through slot words, the record, its placement, data, statics, thread-locals, unwind entries), step 4 behind `BLAZE_LAUNCH=1` (`blaze run` of a binary runs in `blaze-launcher`, unlinked; the daemon still compiles the whole program first), step 5 in a first version (one changed body applied to the running program, anything else a restart in place), the walk's frontier form in the codegen driver (one function ready to compile with no walk; nothing in the daemon calls it yet). Not built - the scan of a thread from outside, lazy serving of needs in the daemon (the seam is written here), placed code kept across runs, test binaries, backtrace names, x86-64 (compiled, never run), domains, promotion."
- [v2/plan/design/explicit-overflow.md](v2/plan/design/explicit-overflow.md) (2026-11-12): "blaze::implicit_overflow: integer + - * << >>, unary -, compound forms and value-losing casts must say what overflow means (checked_*, wrapping_*, saturating_*, overflowing_*, try_from) unless the reach prover shows they fit; one proof, the same in both profiles."
- [v2/plan/design/error-sets.md](v2/plan/design/error-sets.md) (2026-11-12): Error sets (edition change 2, ledger row E3). A function's error type is the exact set of failures it may return, written `A | B` under `#![blaze::error_unions]`. `?` widens a member or a smaller set into a larger one, a set the body's failures do not fit is an error naming the call, the member and the set, a `match` covers every member, and the set costs what the hand-written enum costs. What is built, its floor, and the list of bstd signatures that move onto it.
- [v2/plan/design/effects.md](v2/plan/design/effects.md) (2026-11-12): "#[blaze::expect(..)]: a function says exactly what it does (panic, alloc, block, diverge); what it leaves out is checked absent and what its own list has is checked present, over MIR on pure's walk. The old spellings (nopanic, noalloc, nonblocking), which loops are known to end, and where #[blaze::constant_time] would sit."
- [v2/plan/design/certificate.md](v2/plan/design/certificate.md) (2026-11-12): The request certificate: one store record a request shape and content that says "this request is answered already, by these outputs", checked by the daemon's loop before any plan, view walk or job; the walk is what happens when it does not hold, and it starts at the units that read the input that moved.
- [v2/plan/design/caches.md](v2/plan/design/caches.md) (2026-11-12): The inventory of every place blaze keeps a result to avoid work, with the grain of each key, how it is invalidated and bounded, its defect and owner; and every hash function by use. The `domains` script holds each hash domain and each non-BLAKE3 hasher in the tree to a row here.
- [v2/plan/design/bstd-sim-test.md](v2/plan/design/bstd-sim-test.md) (2026-11-12): The attribute `#[bstd::test]` runs a test shaped like `main` (it takes a `Cx` and an `Io`) on the deterministic simulation under 256 seeds by default, with IO failures, delays and power cuts on unless the test leaves one out by name; a failure prints its seed and a one-line replay command, and the seed replays to the same trace byte for byte. The runner is `blaze_core::sim::seeds`, on the one simulation; bstd adds the attribute and the unwind of a power cut.
- [future/const-macros.md](future/const-macros.md) (2026-11-12): Const macros: proc macros written inline as const fn over flat syntax trees, run by the const evaluator. Experimental.
- [v2/plan/design/tiers.md](v2/plan/design/tiers.md) (2026-11-11): "One build goal, edit or max (D18; step 7 of scheduler.md): what done means for each, how a Cargo profile maps to one, what the status says, and the shape of the two tiers' keys. Built - the goal as one type from --goal to the policy, the goal in the record key, the Finished line. Not built - the goal on the live board, tier 0 for code a package override or std fixes at an LLVM level, optimized code stored by trace, background promotion (deferred; what the patch path lacks is listed)."
- [v2/plan/design/scripts.md](v2/plan/design/scripts.md) (2026-11-11): Python leaves the repository: what was deleted, and Rust scripts run by blaze (`blaze run script.rs`, bstd, typed input, stage 0) replacing the rest.
- [v2/plan/design/scheduler.md](v2/plan/design/scheduler.md) (2026-11-11): The scheduler blaze is moving to: one graph of pure, identity-keyed nodes pulled by what is waited for, cycles as single nodes, no shared mutable state, priority from who waits, memory and cores both admitted, code tiers as nodes, built to scale to hundreds of cores. Replaces the 2026-11-02 plan, with what of it is built and the order of the rest.
- [v2/plan/design/hub.md](v2/plan/design/hub.md) (2026-11-11): The hub keeps warm daemons for many agent lanes. A lane is a root (a BLAKE3 Merkle tree) an agent reads and changes through one API with no checkout; every change is one transaction to a new root, checked at once on a warm machine, the verdict awaited by root. Git stays the origin and the hub is an index of it, every object known by its content id and its git id. Trust, routing, what to measure, adoption, and the order of building.
- [v2/plan/design/debugging.md](v2/plan/design/debugging.md) (2026-11-11): What an agent or a person asking "why was this build slow, wrong or not reused" gets from one command, without reading code, guessing or attaching strace. Fourteen gaps (a to n) that each cost real time on 2026-11-10 and 11, with what closes each and what holds it closed. Each item says whether it is built.
- [v2/plan/design/why.md](v2/plan/design/why.md) (2026-11-10): Why blaze recomputed each step of a build, said after every build and by `blaze why`, as a chain from the step through the key parts that differ down to a real input change (a file, a variable, a flag) or one of a closed set of other terminal reasons; an unexplained recompute is a blaze bug and is counted.
- [v2/plan/design/sys.md](v2/plan/design/sys.md) (2026-11-10): The bottom of bstd (ledger row S4). One crate, blaze-sys, is the only home of system calls (Linux by raw call with no libc, macOS through libSystem, Windows through ntdll and kernel32); the runtime pieces Rust's std provided each get an owner; blaze-core moves onto it call by call behind a ban list that is the progress meter.
- [v2/plan/design/store-pool.md](v2/plan/design/store-pool.md) (2026-11-10): The store's hot tier as a vmcache-style buffer pool - one reserved range with a fixed slot per page of every store file, a state word per page (optimistic and pinned reads), misses as explicit reads around the page cache through blaze-core that the task yields on, immutable records written once through the pool, eviction by the one evictor (a second-chance sweep that takes a page read once first) with MADV_DONTNEED / MADV_FREE_REUSABLE, prefetch we plan ourselves (each view's recorded trace replayed in order and paced by its hits, then the change set's cone in the query graph), codegen outputs then memos then the image on it, a DST, and the lanes.
- [v2/plan/design/std.md](v2/plan/design/std.md) (2026-11-10): blaze's own standard library, written from scratch on core and alloc. No ambient authority (main receives an Io and every function touches only what it is handed), sans-IO underneath (one Io over io_uring, kqueue, IOCP and the simulation), and every blaze crate moves onto it.
- [v2/plan/design/simd.md](v2/plan/design/simd.md) (2026-11-10): Portable SIMD in blaze. The vector types are the pinned nightly's `core::simd`, with no feature gate under `#![blaze::simd]` (the edition turns it on); blaze adds one macro, `simd::native_lanes!`, and `#[blaze::multiversion]`, which compiles a function once per CPU level and picks one when the program starts; how the differentiator and the GPU kernels use the same types.
- [v2/plan/design/records.md](v2/plan/design/records.md) (2026-11-10): Records and named arguments (edition change 4, ledger row E5). Under `#![blaze::records]`, `{ a: T, b: U }` is a structural type (core's `Record` over the tuple of its fields sorted by name), `{ a: x, b }` its value and `{ a, b: p }` its pattern; a record parameter whose fields have defaults is how arguments are named and left out. What the edition page left open is decided here.
- [v2/plan/design/patch-in-place.md](v2/plan/design/patch-in-place.md) (2026-11-10): What a link after a one-function edit costs, step by step, and the design that makes it cost the edit. Built - the link as a patch of its file (ranges written, a Merkle digest of the file), link inputs kept beside the database and brought forward by the build's delta, function, static and span rows kept per image with one keyed Merkle digest as the link's id, and the spans that count each. Not built - the address and perf maps as patches, the writer's tables built by block, the patch regions' room out of the file's length (the compact file, designed here; the room already costs no bytes written, hashed, copied or stored, written 2026-11-11 and not yet built or run).
- [v2/plan/design/ownership.md](v2/plan/design/ownership.md) (2026-11-10): Ownership properties derived by compile-time reflection. One const walk over what a type owns answers reachability questions (`Acyclic`, no capability, no secret, no cell); `where const { COND }` makes a blanket impl of its answer; generic const expressions put arithmetic in types; `Shared` over an acyclic type and `Shares<T, K, N, D>` hold linear values.
- [v2/plan/design/incremental-walk.md](v2/plan/design/incremental-walk.md) (2026-11-10): The codegen step after an edit. Describes are memos; the driver keeps each program's walk (its items, the graph of what each refers to, what the roots reach) and its last `Built` by row, and a build patches both - the walk by the changed describes and a delete-and-re-derive rule over the graph, the `Built` by the rows of what the walk touched - so every pass costs the edit, not the program. Covers what is kept and its keys, each pass's dependency rule, why the patch equals the whole build, the cost of each pass, and what is not built.
- [v2/plan/design/formal-verification.md](v2/plan/design/formal-verification.md) (2026-11-10): The verifier: blaze translates its own borrow-checked MIR to Lean 4 and the pinned Lean checks proofs of specs written once in blaze's extensions. v0 (safe Rust by functional translation) is written in crates/hir-ty-lean with the first proof in the tree; lean/Blaze/Mir is the executable Lean semantics of MIR for a first subset that models, passes and the evaluator are held to, with its trusted base listed; the Verus tier was retired on 2026-11-10. Planned: v1 unsafe and interior mutability in an Iris-style logic, v2 atomics (SC, then RC11), v3 crashes on files and mmap (Perennial-style, sharing the DST's kernel model), v4 compiler correctness. DST stays on everything. A second package, lean/analysis, proves blaze-diff's derivative rules and fast_math rewrites over the reals with Mathlib, from the rule table the Rust differentiator runs.
- [v2/plan/design/facts.md](v2/plan/design/facts.md) (2026-11-10): "Facts: what blaze proves about an item is one record, read by the optimizer and codegen through facts_of and covered by keys. Slice 1 (the record, unwind edges and repeated pure calls in MIR, ProgramLifetime's check, Ref32, three lints) is written and unbuilt; the rest is specified."
- [v2/plan/design/extensions.md](v2/plan/design/extensions.md) (2026-11-10): Extensions. People write MIR lints, facts and transforms as ordinary no_std Rust crates; blaze compiles each from source against its own API crates, checks it is capability-safe, loads it natively into the daemon and runs it under fuel and a capped arena. Slice 1 (the API, the checks, the host loop, the facts fixpoint) is built; the daemon's build of an extension is slice 2.
- [v2/plan/design/early-drop.md](v2/plan/design/early-drop.md) (2026-11-10): Edition change 11, `#![blaze::early_drop]`. A value whose destructor only frees memory is dropped after its last use, not at the end of its scope; guards and everything else keep Rust's drop. Which values, where the drop goes, raw pointers, order, what the borrow checker newly accepts, the `unused_guard` lint, what is built and what is not.
- [v2/plan/design/determinism.md](v2/plan/design/determinism.md) (2026-11-10): Build-time code (build scripts, proc macros, sandboxed tests) is deterministic by construction. The end state is build code with no ambient authority, taking a build handle; until then an existing build.rs runs natively in the OS sandbox with randomness and the wall clock from a provider blaze controls (in blaze's std, at the source), a sandbox backstop that answers what still reaches the kernel, and Linux programs linked with no libc. Three rungs chosen before the build, four lints, `blaze explain build-scripts`, a twice-run check; the wasm rung is specified, not built.
- [v2/plan/design/debug-side-file.md](v2/plan/design/debug-side-file.md) (2026-11-10): A dev build's executable carries no debug info - it is a side file every debugger and std's backtrace find unaided (ELF `<name>.debug` by `.gnu_debuglink` with a CRC that is a function of the build id, Mach-O `<name>.dSYM` by `LC_UUID`), kept as per-function records patched in place; one program is one link however many paths it is placed at. Built - the side file, its model and writer, updates that encode only a link's changed functions, the profile default, one link per unhashed program, a build id of what the image holds and not of its directory, `link write` events by region, the files placed after the answer from bytes the daemon holds (2026-11-11, written, not built or run). Not built - the side file as a store output, the kept image keyed by inputs, the writers' tables by entry, the maps as records, the patch room out of the file (patch-in-place.md). The 162 MB is mostly not debug info - at least 128 MiB is the two patch regions' room.
- [v2/plan/design/ci.md](v2/plan/design/ci.md) (2026-11-10): blaze's own CI in seconds: a pull request is a view on a warm daemon that already holds main's state, on the Mac runner itself and on one long-lived Linux machine, with no VM per job; a fresh ix snapshot per job only for untrusted code. The per-step budget to a check in under 20 s, what blaze must do for it, the trust boundary, and what is built.
- [v2/plan/objectives.md](v2/plan/objectives.md) (2026-11-09): The ledger. Every objective of the plan, the check that decides it and where it stands; generated from objectives.json by scripts/src/bin/ledger.rs.
- [v2/plan/design/tasks.md](v2/plan/design/tasks.md) (2026-11-09): Tasks in the agent app. Every agent belongs to a task, the sidebar lists tasks with their agents under them, and a task says what it waits on, what it costs and how it ended.
- [v2/plan/design/reflect.md](v2/plan/design/reflect.md) (2026-11-09): Twelve things built as libraries on compile-time reflection (keys that cannot miss a field, checked persisted layouts, reachability assertions, state-keeping hot reload, pure functions as cached queries, record and replay, contracts as property tests, derived layouts, tree operations, memory by type, one outward schema, UI from types), where each lives, what it waits on and the order.
- [v2/plan/design/lir.md](v2/plan/design/lir.md) (2026-11-09): LIR, blaze's own low-level IR, replaces Cranelift IR as the one input of code generation (Andrew's decisions, 2026-11-09) - its level (after layout, ABI and drop elaboration, before instruction selection), columnar encoding, types and operations, how it carries Rust's facts (rustc's set: noalias, nonnull, alignment, ranges, provenance, atomic orderings, volatile; no TBAA) as promises a consumer may drop and meanings it must keep, intrinsics and SIMD, unwinding, debug info, inline asm, references by place, its key and its blaze-format record; its consumers (stencils keyed on LIR ops, LLVM lowered from LIR directly, blaze's wasm emitter; Cranelift left only inside Wasmtime); LLVM's own allocations routed through blaze's allocator with a context per compile and charged to the unit's task; const eval staying on MIR; why a new IR and not lowered MIR, against codegen_ssa, CLIF, LLVM IR, GIMPLE/RTL, Zig's AIR, Go's SSA and MLIR; the migration straight to LIR with no bridge (lanes written in parallel, one switch gated on blaze building blaze and the real projects passing, then the deletions); ranked risks; the decisions that settled its open questions (no TBAA, no stored LIR, no extra facts and no folding until after the switch).
- [v2/plan/design/edition.md](v2/plan/design/edition.md) (2026-11-09): The blaze edition. Rust with eleven opt-in changes (handles that copy themselves, error unions, view types, records, contexts, effects at the border, values that must be used up, contracts and pattern types, compile-time reflection, `&uniq`, early drop), what it removes, the lints that get a crate ready for it, and the order it is built in.
- [v2/plan/design/comptime.md](v2/plan/design/comptime.md) (2026-11-09): Compile-time reflection in blaze. Phase 1 completes nightly `core::mem::type_info` in blaze's const evaluator; phase 2 is the opt-in `blaze_comptime` extension (`for const f in fields_of::<T>()`, `self.[f]`, `for<F: Field<T>>` bounds, `fn_info`), and 2b adds `dyn` and fn-pointer calls in const checked at evaluation and `const static { .. }` blocks that run any code at compile time; phase 3 builds types from const code (`type_of!`).
- [v2/plan/bounds.md](v2/plan/bounds.md) (2026-11-09): Every speed-of-light bound blaze is held to, one machine-read block each; harness/v2/bounds.py reads this file and budgets.py measures it.
- [v2/plan.md](v2/plan.md) (2026-11-09): The plan for blaze, whole, on one page. The goal, the rules, the one design every part shares, the targets, and how the work is run; the ledger of objectives is plan/objectives.md.
- [memory-footprint.md](memory-footprint.md) (2026-11-09): Why a stage5 self-build's daemon reached 75.7 GiB against a 47 GiB limit on the Mac (freed memory pinned by long-lived blocks on the same heap, query storage that only grows, two measures of memory), and the fix: an owner per lifetime (frames reset per item, outputs as records in the store's own vmcache-style buffer pool), footprint as the one measure, telemetry first.
- [v2/plan/admission-by-footprint.md](v2/plan/admission-by-footprint.md) (2026-11-06): admission by footprint (lane admit-footprint-1106, 2026-11-06) - the plane admits against the process footprint plus grants not yet realized, not grants alone; freed-but-kept allocator memory is purged before work is refused or the daemon dies; a task that alone passes the ceiling fails with a typed error naming it; grants are graded against peaks; every task span names its kind, crate and unit; proved by a blaze-sim DST with planted bugs.
- [future/gpu/shaders.md](future/gpu/shaders.md) (2026-11-06): Vertex and fragment shaders, and compute kernels with inline ray query, written in Rust and compiled by blaze (MIR to naga IR, then MSL, SPIR-V or WGSL), replacing the harness app's Slang, with a binding table generated from the Rust signatures.
- [v2/plan/design/named-locks.md](v2/plan/design/named-locks.md) (2026-11-05): Every lock in blaze is a named blaze_core::lock::{Lock, ReadLock, Signal} that records who waited, behind whom and for how long, on the slow path only; raw std and parking_lot locks are banned; the profile ranks locks by wait time (`lock_waits`, `blaze debug locks`) and the gate fails a build where one lock eats a share of worker time.
- [v2/plan/design/explore-generic.md](v2/plan/design/explore-generic.md) (2026-11-05): The explorer for any program that emits blaze telemetry, not just the blaze daemon. ix-prof gains the one serving side (feature `explore`, the WebTransport server, certificate, link, token and live stream moved out of blaze-explore) behind a `Source` trait; the protocol speaks of generic things (processes, threads, open spans, tasks with state, progress and a "waiting on", task edges); build steps, crates and build scripts are the `blaze` layer on top, and the daemon is one `Source`. Covers the tables, versions and the gate that keeps ix.dev/explore from falling behind, the page's Running now and Graph views, and the order of the work.
- [v2/plan/design/explore-core.md](v2/plan/design/explore-core.md) (2026-11-05): The explorer's core moves to Rust compiled to wasm32 by blaze (`blaze-explore-core`), the crate the daemon, the build's live view and `blaze status` already share (`blaze_protocol::now`) plus the wire decoding and the trace's aggregation and layout; the page (indexable-inc/ix) keeps only the shell. The producer serves its own core over the session, so page and producer can never disagree on a schema. Each view is written from a question a person asks (is it stuck, what is slow, why did this rerun, where is X and what does it wait on), not from the tables a producer happens to have.
- [v2/plan/design/build-view.md](v2/plan/design/build-view.md) (2026-11-05): The live view of `blaze build`, `check` and `test`, redesigned. One typed model of a build as it runs now (`blaze_protocol::now::Now`: its phase, the daemon's memory against its ceiling and how pressed it is, busy and idle workers with their innermost spans, what the rest waits on and what each blocker holds back, downloads, the slowest so far, how long nothing moved), folded by one sans-IO core from the plane's graph records, the threads' open spans and the downloads, and read by the build's own client, `blaze status` and the explorer's daemon source. Drawn by blaze-screen (docs/terminal.md).
- [memory-pool.md](memory-pool.md) (2026-11-05): The long-term memory design. One budget per machine, run like a database buffer pool. Every byte is charged to a task's frame or to a named cache. Admission uses measured peaks by kind and input size. Every cache is an evictable hot tier over the content-addressed store, with one evictor. Nothing is buffered without a bound. One daemon per machine, and the kernel's limit as the backstop.
- [memory-budget.md](memory-budget.md) (2026-11-05): Memory as a scheduled budget: blaze reads the machine's real limit, admits work by its measured peak, sheds caches under pressure and stops with an error naming what cannot fit, never swapping a machine to death.
- [v2/plan/design/vfs-sync.md](v2/plan/design/vfs-sync.md) (2026-11-04): blaze v2 vfs - the team's source of truth lives on Cloudflare (a Rust Worker built by blaze, run as wasm, a Durable Object per head); multiplayer edits and merges are operations on the syntax tree, not text; jj-style changes with stable IDs, first-class conflicts and an operation log; a branch can stack on another and takes its updates automatically; Pando-style per-head ordering for thousands of agents; blaze builds straight from a synced head; git is only a mirror.
- [v2/plan/design/structured-output.md](v2/plan/design/structured-output.md) (2026-11-04): "Everything blaze says to a person or an agent becomes data first: a `Report` (headline, rule, facts, fixes, blocks, causes) in one crate, `blaze-report`, carried by the daemon's API as CBOR and drawn by one pure renderer as styled text, plain text or JSON; the rendering rules, the build-script `cargo:blaze-report=` directive, `blaze explain`, terminal capabilities and the `[terminal]` config, the progress and summary design for the next slice, and the inventory of what is left to port (2026-11-04, lane structured-output: errors through `ApiError`, the build-script failure, the llvm-sys pin and the sandbox's directive refusal are ported)."
- [v2/plan/design/no-tracing.md](v2/plan/design/no-tracing.md) (2026-11-04): blaze drops the `tracing` crate. Every span and event goes through blaze's own recorder in a new leaf crate `blaze-trace`: one registry for span and event kinds, `span!` and `event!` macros with static call sites, words written straight into the flight ring (no dispatcher, no visitor). The doc gives the grammar, the slot-reuse ordering, the cost budget with its instruction-count bench on the Linux bench runners, the mapping from each tracing form, vendor patch series for third-party crates, a lockfile ban in `blaze check`, and the lanes parallel agents take.
- [v2/plan/design/name-free-identity.md](v2/plan/design/name-free-identity.md) (2026-11-04): Unison-style identities for blaze. A compiled body's store key holds what it does, never what it or its callees are called or where they are written. A name or place is keyed only by code that reads it. Positions are held by table and filled per instance, and the link keeps per-body identity.
- [v2/plan/design/multiconfig-check.md](v2/plan/design/multiconfig-check.md) (2026-11-04): "One `blaze check` over every configuration of a package at once (its targets, feature sets and platforms), and the reachability lints that gives: `blaze::dead` (no configuration uses the item; rustc's `dead_code` over all of them), `blaze::test_only` (only the tests do; `--fix` adds `#[cfg(test)]`) and `blaze::cfg_only` (only some features or platforms do; the narrowest exact `#[cfg]`). Slice 1 is built (2026-11-04, lane multiconfig-check: the host's targets under the features asked for, the three lints, the `#[cfg]` fix with a soundness check); multi-platform and feature-set configurations, tagging every diagnostic with its configurations, and dependency findings are designed here and left."
- [v2/plan/design/lock-policy.md](v2/plan/design/lock-policy.md) (2026-11-04): lock policy (lane lock-policy, 2026-11-04, approved by Andrew) - CI refuses any change to the lock files, naming each move, why and the fix; locally a build writes them but never silently; `blaze.lock` beside `Cargo.lock` pins the blaze release and its nightly, the index's newest publish time and every pinned native input's digests; `lock = required` refuses locally too and blaze's tree sets it; what is built and what is left.
- [v2/plan/design/http3-sans-io.md](v2/plan/design/http3-sans-io.md) (2026-11-04): blaze's QUIC and WebTransport stack becomes sans-IO cores with thin drivers, on rustls. quinn-proto stays as the QUIC core; a new HTTP/3 + WebTransport core in blaze-http (static-only QPACK, SETTINGS, extended CONNECT, WebTransport streams and datagrams) drives it; one tokio driver owns the UDP socket and the timers behind the same driver contract as HTTP/1. quinn, quinn-udp, wtransport and wtransport-proto leave the graph. Covers what blaze uses QUIC for, the contracts, the browser's requirements, the losing designs, migration and tests.
- [v2/plan/design/deadline-waits.md](v2/plan/design/deadline-waits.md) (2026-11-04): Every blocking kernel wait goes through one blaze-core primitive that takes an absolute deadline on the injected clock and recomputes the time left on every retry; the profile sampler stops interrupting threads with signals; a stuck daemon start names the span it is stuck in.
- [profiling.md](profiling.md) (2026-11-04): blaze's one profiler (lane observe; a plan until each part it describes lands), one span stream into one buffer with several readers. The schema (spans, counters, builds, processes, test_runs, samples, images, provenance, inputs, alloc_samples, heap_by_owner, panics; Arrow, defined once in crates/blaze-profile/src/schema.rs), the flight recorder, the Parquet history with `blaze debug sql` and `nix run .#duckdb`, the client's rows in it, the live feed (`blaze debug live`, the explorer), the stall watchdog, and `BLAZE_PROFILE` as an export from the history.
- [v2/plan/design/verify.md](v2/plan/design/verify.md) (2026-11-02): How blaze checks its own store and incremental builds: BLAZE_VERIFY_STORE recomputes a sampled fraction of store hits and compares bytes, and a property-test edit fuzzer holds every incremental build to a clean one through the invalidation oracle (blaze-v2-proof).
- [v2/plan/design/vecreport.md](v2/plan/design/vecreport.md) (2026-11-02): Lint `blaze::vecreport` - report what LLVM's optimized code still does in a loop (a bounds, overflow or panic check that survived, a loop left scalar and why) at the source line, read from the IR after every pass and the loop vectorizer's remarks, hot loops only under a profile; prior art, the design, the guarantee it rests on, and what the stencil tier can say.
- [v2/plan/design/toolchain-c.md](v2/plan/design/toolchain-c.md) (2026-11-02): blaze uses only its own pinned LLVM and ships one pinned C toolchain built from it (clang, lld, compiler-rt, libc++, wasi-libc, libc stubs), so no compiler, sysroot, SDK or runtime the machine installed changes what blaze builds; rustup and the nightly download go.
- [v2/plan/design/tail-calls.md](v2/plan/design/tail-calls.md) (2026-11-02): lane tailcall: `become` (explicit_tail_calls) as a guaranteed tail call through the front end, the MIR evaluator, the stencils and LLVM; dev code is stencils, which make one, and wasm refuses it by name.
- [v2/plan/design/storemodel.md](v2/plan/design/storemodel.md) (2026-11-02): lane storemodel's model checker of the store and kernel protocol (crate blaze-storemodel): the real blaze-cas Store, Writers and Kernel driven through every schedule of a few actors, a crash after every IO step on a file system that models what a crash keeps, and a restore checked against six properties.
- [v2/plan/design/specialization.md](v2/plan/design/specialization.md) (2026-11-02): Sound specialization as an opt-in blaze extension, `#![blaze::specialization]` with `#[blaze::specialization_trait]`, built on rustc's always-applicable rule (min_specialization) without its unsafe markers; rustc's min_specialization checks are ported for std and the crates that enable the feature.
- [v2/plan/design/sealed-orphan.md](v2/plan/design/sealed-orphan.md) (2026-11-02): Relaxing the orphan rule soundly as an opt-in blaze extension: `#[blaze::sealed]` traits whose crate may write `impl<T: Sealed> ForeignTrait for T` (built, with its checks in `hir-ty-coherence`), and the ranked alternatives, including a whole-workspace coherence domain (designed, not built).
- [v2/plan/design/pure-fns.md](v2/plan/design/pure-fns.md) (2026-11-02): "#[blaze::pure] and #[blaze::pure(trusted = ..)]: functions that read the world only through their arguments, checked transitively over MIR; what counts as observing an address, which std calls are allowed, and the memory and purity facts every function gets."
- [v2/plan/design/polymorph.md](v2/plan/design/polymorph.md) (2026-11-02): Polymorphization in blaze v2 (lane polymorph, 2026-11-02) - one copy of a generic instance for every set of type arguments its code can't tell apart (unused, used only by size and alignment, used only through a table), decided by the share key before codegen; ADT facts become structural shapes, codegen-answered calls are keyed by full identity, what rustc's polymorphization did and why it was removed, the guarantee relied on, the dictionary-passing design left for later, and how it is measured.
- [v2/plan/design/perf-history.md](v2/plan/design/perf-history.md) (2026-11-02): Performance history of the programs blaze builds (lane perf-history). Each profiled run is one row set in the profile history (the run with its exact tree, blaze, binary and host; per function self and total samples, by path and by code identity), and `blaze perf diff <run> [<base>]` gives per function the change in time with a noise bound and the cause class read from the identities (its code changed, built with other settings, a callee changed, or same code and callees). Built: the code map each link writes, the rows and their Parquet round trip, the identity join, the diff (text and JSON) and `blaze perf record|runs|diff`. Designed: the `--prof` switch that records on its own, call and instruction counts.
- [v2/plan/design/lint-borrow-workarounds.md](v2/plan/design/lint-borrow-workarounds.md) (2026-11-02): blaze's `blaze::borrow_workaround` and `blaze::nll_workaround` — code written around a weaker borrow checker than blaze's (a second lookup, a clone to end a borrow, an index loop for a cursor, take and put back), found only when the direct form passes blaze's checker on the rewritten MIR and behaves the same; what is built (the double lookup), how a rewrite is checked, how published crates are kept building on stable Rust, and the shapes still to build.
- [v2/plan/design/linear.md](v2/plan/design/linear.md) (2026-11-02): "#[blaze::linear]: a type whose values may not be dropped implicitly, checked on built MIR with the borrow check; generic code admits one only through a `#[blaze::linear]` type parameter, `Option` and `Result` do, and an error exit abandons a value through its type's `Drop`."
- [v2/plan/design/kernel.md](v2/plan/design/kernel.md) (2026-11-02): blaze v2's kernel: registered pure compute steps from MIR down, each value kept in the store under its identity, its step's code and flags, with the narrow reads it made and their hashes, verified on lookup; codegen's dev templates are its first entries.
- [v2/plan/design/icf.md](v2/plan/design/icf.md) (2026-11-02): Identical code folding in blaze v2 (lane icf, 2026-11-02) - equal instances are one before codegen (the share key) and one after it (dedupe by code ID, relocations by what they name, to a bounded fixpoint), the linker given one copy with every relocation renamed to it, statics included; what never folds, the guarantee relied on, and how it is measured.
- [v2/plan/design/heap-to-stack.md](v2/plan/design/heap-to-stack.md) (2026-11-02): HeapToStack, blaze's own MIR pass: a Box::new, Rc::new or small vec! whose allocation never leaves its function lives in the function's frame instead, only in programs whose allocator is std's, capped per value and per frame, and never in a frame that can recur.
- [v2/plan/design/field-order.md](v2/plan/design/field-order.md) (2026-11-02): Field order by heat (lane fieldorder, 2026-11-02) - the fields a profile shows hot code reading laid out first in `repr(Rust)` structs and enum variants, only when the type keeps rustc's size, alignment, ABI, niche and tag; the Reference text that allows it, what is never reordered, the heat estimate from built MIR weighted by PGO counts, the plan input and its place in layout identity, the tests, the benchmark, and the driver hook still to add.
- [v2/plan/design/doctests.md](v2/plan/design/doctests.md) (2026-11-02): "Doctests built and run by blaze with its own front end, never rustdoc: rustdoc's rules for finding examples, writing their programs (line-aligned to the docs) and judging them, ported; each example is its own unit (its own crate, binary and process, patched on an edit like any blaze test), never merged, in any edition; what is built (2026-11-02, lanes doctest to doctest5: `blaze test --doc` builds each example as its own crate in parallel, builds and links only an edited one while every other is found unchanged by one store lookup, builds `test_harness` examples as tests, and runs each in its own process) and what is left."
- [v2/plan/design/devirt.md](v2/plan/design/devirt.md) (2026-11-02): Whole-program devirtualization. A final binary's walk lists every vtable the program makes, and the program's facts are closed per object type. A MIR pass then turns `dyn` calls into direct calls (one type) or vtable compares (two to four), keyed by the facts each body read. A second walk lists the new direct callees. Covers what makes a set closed, the guarantees relied on, vtable identity, and the PGO producer still to build.
- [v2/plan/design/contracts.md](v2/plan/design/contracts.md) (2026-11-02): Function contracts (nightly's `#![feature(contracts)]`) in blaze — the same as the pinned nightly first, then checked by default in dev and test profiles, tested by generated blaze-sim property tests, proved in Lean (formal-verification.md; the Z3 tier was retired on 2026-11-10), and used by the optimizer only once proved.
- [v2/plan/design/constspec.md](v2/plan/design/constspec.md) (2026-11-02): Specializing functions on constant arguments (lane constspec, 2026-11-02) - a MIR pass that lists the calls passing a constant their callee branches on, and a copy of the callee compiled knowing it with the decided branches gone, which the code generator calls; when a call gets one, the budgets that bound the program's copies, why `#[inline(never)]` callees get copies and addressed or exported ones do not, the keys, the guarantees relied on, and the benchmark.
- [v2/plan/design/code-layout.md](v2/plan/design/code-layout.md) (2026-11-02): Profile-guided code layout in blaze's own linker: C3 function order from an ix-prof sampling profile mapped back through per-build address maps, cold functions inferred without a profile and placed last, cold blocks weighted unlikely; hot/cold splitting designed, not built; the benchmark.
- [v2/plan/design/code-identity.md](v2/plan/design/code-identity.md) (2026-11-02): The one definition of code identity in blaze (crates/hir-ty-identity). Compile identity is what one instance's generated code depends on; behaviour identity (CodeId) is what running it can depend on. Both are Merkle graphs with recursion hashed as one strongly connected component. Every other hash of code ports onto them and is deleted.
- [v2/plan/design/clone-out.md](v2/plan/design/clone-out.md) (2026-11-02): Lane clone-out: a second checkout's build directory costs only its own bytes, because every output of 16 KiB or more is a clone of the store's read-only copy, and each build reports the bytes it cloned, wrote and copied.
- [v2/plan/design/borrowck-cursor.md](v2/plan/design/borrowck-cursor.md) (2026-11-02): BLAZE_BORROWCK=polonius-flow, a borrow-check mode that accepts what datalog Polonius accepts and the alpha rejects (linked-list cursors, flow-sensitive invariance), and never less than the alpha.
- [v2/plan/design/bits.md](v2/plan/design/bits.md) (2026-11-02): `#[blaze::bits]`: Zig-style bit-packed structs with ordinary field syntax. Layout is the backing integer's; a field's width comes from its type; field places stay places through borrow checking and are lowered to integer ops by one MIR pass at the end of the runtime passes, so neither the interpreter nor the code generator sees a new projection.
- [v2/plan/design/arbitrary-ints.md](v2/plan/design/arbitrary-ints.md) (2026-11-02): Integers of any width, `u1`..`u128` and `i1`..`i128`, as Zig has them, behind the crate attribute `#![blaze::arbitrary_ints]`. They are real primitive types, shadowed like `u8`. They are stored in the smallest power-of-two container with the unused high bits as a niche, overflow at their width, and get their trait impls from blanket impls in core over a solver-builtin marker trait.
- [ix-prof-format.md](ix-prof-format.md) (2026-11-02): The ix-prof profile format and interfaces. Covers the .ixprof container (canonical JSON manifest, Arrow IPC tables, blake3 id), the tables, symbols, pprof and Chrome exports, the /debug/pprof endpoints, the live stream with cursors, gaps and drop counts, and the design for profiling any blaze-built program with no code changes.
- [future/gpu/raytracing.md](future/gpu/raytracing.md) (2026-11-02): Ray tracing in blaze GPU kernels, built on inline ray query, typed pipeline payloads and acceleration structures that carry lifetimes.
- [future/gpu/plan.md](future/gpu/plan.md) (2026-11-02): Rust kernels in the same crate as the host code, compiled by blaze for Metal, Vulkan, CUDA and the CPU, launched through one typed API.
- [future/gpu/README.md](future/gpu/README.md) (2026-11-02): Index of the plans for compiling Rust kernels to GPUs with blaze.
- [future/bootstrap.md](future/bootstrap.md) (2026-11-02): Bootstrap blaze from a wasm seed (blaze's own source plus blaze compiled to core WebAssembly), so blaze is built only by its seed and by blaze, never rustc or cargo, and its source may use blaze-only Rust.
- [future/autodiff.md](future/autodiff.md) (2026-11-02): Differentiation in blaze on CPU and GPU, from automatic differentiation on MIR, to symbolic derivatives of pure functions, to e-graph simplification shared by both.
- [v2/plan/design/store.md](v2/plan/design/store.md) (2026-11-01): blaze v2: the store.
- [v2/plan/design/proc-macros.md](v2/plan/design/proc-macros.md) (2026-11-01): How blaze v2 expands proc macros (a wasm32-wasip1 module under Wasmtime behind the proc_macro bridge, the MIR evaluator as its reference), keys and keeps the expansions, and what it does to be the fastest.
- [v2/plan/design/profile-history.md](v2/plan/design/profile-history.md) (2026-10-31): lane observe, step 3: the flight recorder's Parquet history, its errors table and `blaze debug diff` (crates/blaze-profile/src/history.rs), the DuckDB views and named queries over it (sql/views.sql, sql/examples.sql, src/views.rs), `blaze debug sql` running the pinned DuckDB CLI (src/sql.rs), and the flush's speed of light.
- [v2/plan/design/may-suspend.md](v2/plan/design/may-suspend.md) (2026-10-31): lane may-suspend (2026-10-31): blaze rejects a value held across a call that may park a fiber when that value must not cross threads (`!Send`, or `#[must_not_suspend]`); may-suspend is inferred from the monomorphized call graph from corosensei's `Yielder::suspend`, written only as `#[blaze::may_suspend]` on a trait method or fn-pointer field. Crate `hir-ty-suspend`; replaces sched phase 2's hand audit.
- [v2/plan/design/fibers.md](v2/plan/design/fibers.md) (2026-10-31): lane sched (2026-10-31): a waiting job never blocks its thread, and the scheduler is a sans-IO state machine. Phase 1 is the synchronous core in crates/blaze-graph/src/sched/ with its property tests (written); phase 2 is stackful fibers (corosensei, decided 18:29): the driver and the query-wait hook are written, the pump's replacement and the thread-local audit follow.
- [v2/plan/design/explore.md](v2/plan/design/explore.md) (2026-10-31): the explorer's daemon side (crate blaze-explore), one source of the general profile explorer beside ixprof files and live programs: an HTTP/3 WebTransport server on 127.0.0.1 that https://ix.dev/explore connects to pinning a 13-day self-signed P-256 certificate by hash; the link, origin and token rules, certificate rotation, the ops and the live stream, the WebTransport probe, and the speed of light of live and tiles.
- [v2/plan/design/item-hash.md](v2/plan/design/item-hash.md) (2026-10-30): blaze v2's item identities: a body's type check, MIR and borrow check are filed in the store under an a-priori hash of everything they read (its own name-resolved HIR with no spans, the signature hashes of what it names, the crate's inputs) plus a constructive trace of the global facts they read (impl sets, method candidates, field names, constant values), so a result is a store read with no deep verify, shared across branches, machines and reverted edits; the hash is anonymous (Unison-style), with names and positions in a presentation layer, locations as a per-crate data table, debug info off the edit path, and item IDs in blaze's own reports.
- [v2/plan/design/dbsp.md](v2/plan/design/dbsp.md) (2026-10-30): Push-based incremental name resolution, impl tables and trait candidate sets (lane dbsp). The relations are views maintained on the write side by deltas, DBSP-style, and published as salsa inputs, one per slice, so an edit costs work proportional to the facts it changes and a reader sees a change only when its slice changed.
- [v2/plan/design/caching.md](v2/plan/design/caching.md) (2026-10-30): blaze v2's cache keys name content and relative layout only, never where a checkout, home, target directory, registry or toolchain is; every layer (toolchain, load, macro expansions, build scripts, codegen, the link manifest) is looked up before the work it saves, and a hit is what a rebuild would make.
- [v2/plan/design/vfs.md](v2/plan/design/vfs.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 vfs lane's design: the Merkle tree, heads and views, rebase, the journal with group commit, recovery and compaction, and the disk watcher as one input of transactions.
- [v2/plan/design/unsafe.md](v2/plan/design/unsafe.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: unsafe where it makes code measurably faster, safe Rust everywhere else, and every unsafe line proved sound by our own tools (a Miri of our own, sanitizers in our code generator, model checking).
- [v2/plan/design/restore.md](v2/plan/design/restore.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: the daemon restores from disk instantly: a mapped image with no deserializing, IDs stable across restarts, changed files known from the OS's journal, and work paged in on demand.
- [v2/plan/design/model-checker.md](v2/plan/design/model-checker.md) (2026-10-29): lane safety's model checker for lock-free code (crate blaze-check): shim atomics, locks and threads as coroutines on one OS thread, loom's bounded DPOR over interleavings, every value a load may read under C11, and a model test per lock-free structure against a sequential model.
- [v2/plan/design/memory.md](v2/plan/design/memory.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 manages memory like a game engine: allocators by lifetime (frame, request, view, image), virtual-memory-reserved arenas with stable addresses, pools, generational handles, per-subsystem budgets, and zero general-purpose allocations in the warm loop.
- [v2/plan/design/frontend.md](v2/plan/design/frontend.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: what rust-analyzer's front end got wrong for a compiler, and what v2 does instead: incremental name resolution, indexed impls, one token format, signature-only dependencies, mapped files, no IDE-only work.
- [v2/plan/design/data.md](v2/plan/design/data.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: data-oriented layout and compression in every stage.
- [v2/plan/design/concurrency.md](v2/plan/design/concurrency.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: how threads share data: reads never lock or write shared memory, values are immutable once published, task boundaries reclaim memory, no build lock.
- [v2/plan/design/compile-time.md](v2/plan/design/compile-time.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: the bigger changes for the fastest compile times: reachability-only codegen, a persistent trait cache, the nightly's own solver, proc macros on our own compiler, tiered compilation and idle cores always working, lazy per-function compilation, copy-and-patch codegen, no link and no rewrite for dev runs, one global cache, semantic edits and declared intent, shared generic code, exact test selection, hash-consing, premapped dependencies, scheduling from history, PGO and BOLT.
- [v2/plan/design/codegen.md](v2/plan/design/codegen.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 codegen lane's design: per-function units, instance keys, templates (the back-end memo up to callee renaming), code dedupe, folding by constants, settings and tiering, release summaries and imports.
- [remote-cache.md](remote-cache.md) (2026-10-27): One shared remote cache for CI and everyone: the gateway, the CAS API, and the slices built and to come.

## Records

Research, reports and measurements, true on their date and not brought up to date. Newest first.

- [language.md](language.md) (2026-11-12): Each language change of Rust 1.80 to 1.100 checked against blaze's front end on 2026-11-12, with the test that holds it and what was fixed or is still missing.
- [v2/plan/design/verus.md](v2/plan/design/verus.md) (2026-11-10): The spec form blaze kept from lane verus (Verus's clause syntax as native grammar, gated by `#![feature(blaze_verify)]`, lowered to clause groups in hir-def), and the record of the Z3 tier that proved it until 2026-11-10, when it was retired for Lean.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) (2026-11-03): Changelog: every user-visible change, by release, with [Unreleased] on top.
- [support.md](support.md) (2026-10-30): What blaze v1 supported, cell by cell, each pointing at the report or harness run behind it. v2 has none of these measurements yet.
- [platforms.md](platforms.md) (2026-10-30): The state of each platform under blaze v1 (rustc's link line, the splice, `blaze-engine weaken`), from v1's last CI run that covered them all. v2 has not been run on any platform yet.
- [fn-cache.md](fn-cache.md) (2026-10-30): #[blaze::cache]: results of pure functions kept across runs, keyed by the code they reach. Its library crates were deleted on 2026-10-30.
- [doc.md](doc.md) (2026-10-30): blaze doc as blaze v1 did it (the engine's doc.rs, over a workspace loaded into rust-analyzer): HTML documentation written from the front end's HIR, with no rustdoc. v2 has no `blaze doc` yet.
- [rename.md](rename.md) (2026-10-28): The rename from ra-jit and cargo blaze to blaze (#270), and what its script, tools/rename.py (deleted 2026-11-11), changed.
- [results.md](results.md) (2026-10-27): Results: every number with the harness, commit and report it came from.
- [flat-syntax.md](flat-syntax.md) (2026-10-22): Flat syntax trees for files nobody edits (#42): the design and its memory and time, measured.
